question.prompt:
The edges of a regular tetrahedron with vertices \(A,\) \(B,\) \(C,\) and \(D\) each have length one. Find the least possible distance between a pair of points \(P\) and \(Q,\) where \(P\) is on edge \(AB\) and \(Q\) is on edge \(CD.\)

[Figure 1](figures/1979_AMC_12_Q23_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
The equal edges suggest using midpoints, because a median to the base of an isosceles triangle is perpendicular to that base. Let \(M\) and \(N\) be the midpoints of \(AB\) and \(CD\), respectively.

Since \(AC=BC\) and \(AD=BD\), the medians \(CM\) and \(DM\) are both perpendicular to \(AB\). They are two intersecting lines in plane \(MCD\), so \(AB\) is perpendicular to that plane. Consequently, for every \(Q\) on \(CD\), we have \(AB\perp MQ\).

The Pythagorean theorem in triangles \(AMC\) and \(AMD\) gives
\[
CM^2=DM^2=1-\left(\frac12\right)^2=\frac34.
\]
Thus triangle \(CMD\) is isosceles. Its median \(MN\) is perpendicular to \(CD\), and
\[
MN^2=CM^2-CN^2
=\frac34-\frac14=\frac12.
\]
These perpendiculars show why the midpoints give the minimum. For any permitted \(P\) and \(Q\), applying the Pythagorean theorem twice yields
\[
PQ^2=PM^2+MQ^2
=PM^2+NQ^2+MN^2
\geq\frac12.
\]
The identities remain valid when \(P=M\) or \(Q=N\), with the corresponding term equal to zero. Equality holds exactly when \(P=M\) and \(Q=N\), which are allowed points on the edges. Therefore the least distance is \(\boxed{\frac{\sqrt2}{2}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
solutions.title: Use the midpoints of opposite edges

solutions.explanation:
Choose coordinates that place the two opposite edges in perpendicular horizontal directions, at different heights. Set \(a=\sqrt2/2\) and take
\[
\begin{aligned}
A&=(-\tfrac12,0,0),& B&=(\tfrac12,0,0),\\
C&=(0,-\tfrac12,a),& D&=(0,\tfrac12,a).
\end{aligned}
\]
This represents a regular tetrahedron of side one: \(AB=CD=1\), while each of the other four edges has squared length
\[
\left(\frac12\right)^2+
\left(\frac12\right)^2+a^2
=\frac14+\frac14+\frac12=1.
\]
Every point on \(AB\) has the form \(P=(s,0,0)\), and every point on \(CD\) has the form \(Q=(0,t,a)\), where
\[
-\frac12\leq s,t\leq\frac12.
\]
The spatial distance formula, obtained by applying the Pythagorean theorem in perpendicular directions, gives
\[
PQ^2=s^2+t^2+a^2
=s^2+t^2+\frac12\geq\frac12.
\]
Both squares vanish exactly when \(s=t=0\), and these values lie in the allowed intervals. They select the two edge midpoints. Hence the least possible distance is \(\boxed{\frac{\sqrt2}{2}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
